the governance attributes of the Australian Alps social-ecological landscape system are currently constraining the system's adaptive capacity and that this is having a negative impact on biodiversity outcomes.

(1) governance influences on landscape-scale biodiversity are likely to be complex and context-specific; (2) governance attributes can be specified to support adaptive capacity; and (3) the application of joint SES and scenarios analyses can identify how governance attributes influence landscape-scale biodiversity.

the current governance arrangements in the Australian Alps have the potential to maintain the current level of biodiversity outcomes, but only under a narrow range of future social, ecological and economic drivers.
